issues.reason: Names and casing bars derivation across parts of speech ('Inflection only — never derivation'), so the event-noun 'death' keeps its own form; 'die' is a different word.

Core patterns projects only a definite referent's Member / Name typing atom out of a seal ('The event class and every role atom always stay inside'), so a top-level (Patient sk_die_1 sk_boy_1) over-projects role structure that belongs inside the sealed complement.

Propositional attitudes: 'A control verb with a to-infinitive never seals — sealing is finite-clause-only'; want + to-infinitive takes the non-finite-complement pattern (complement reified as sibling atoms, attached by Theme, no tense of its own, controller's role copied in).

This mistakes the reviewer's own gap 2 for a defect: an Implication is a statement needing its own STV and has no licensed placement inside a seal, so the group witness is graceful improvisation in gap territory and every atom it carries is true of the sentence.

Categorical statements: 'A property of a plural's members is never predicated of the group symbol ... a bare (Member <group> <prop>) appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself', and being held responsible is member-level.

The atom demanded would be (Member sk_people_1 involved) — the very group-level predication the plural rule forbids (see issue 4) — and the distributive route that would license it has no placement inside a seal, so omitting it is the only non-violating option.

Status predicates: 'An appositive ... has no tense of its own: its typing atom takes the host clause's wrapper — past host → (Past ...)', and tense wraps a Measure exactly like a copular atom, so the age under the past 'said' host needs the Past wrapper.

gaps_confirmed: 'hold NP + predicative adjective' ('held responsible') — an ascription that neither the resultative shape (which requires the object to change) nor the impersonal-reported-attitude template squarely covers
a universal quantifier ('everyone') inside a sealed complement — the prescribed Implication rule form has no defined placement inside a seal
a possessive genitive on a deverbal nominalization naming its undergoer ('his son's death') — the complements section covers only the of-phrase object case
new_gaps: a member-level copular property of a plural inside a seal has NO licensed carrier at all: the distributive rule cannot be placed inside a seal and the flat group atom is forbidden, which is what forces dropping the atom rather than adding one

'his son' is never typed or linked (only the coreferent boy witness survives), because a kinship genitive inside a seal projects only its typing atom and the instruction set does not say which of 'son' / 'boy' that typing should use
repair_summary: Relemmatized the event-noun to 'death' (symbol sk_death_1) at top level and inside the seal. Moved (Patient sk_death_1 sk_boy_1) inside the sealed complement, leaving only the projected typing atom at top level. Unsealed the want-complement: the hold event's atoms are now siblings inside the say-seal with (Theme sk_want_1 sk_hold_1) and no tense of its own. Dropped (Member sk_people_1 responsible). Wrapped the appositive age as (Past (Measure terrance_cottrell_sr age 33 year)).
notes: The group encoding of 'everyone involved' is kept deliberately — inside a seal the universal's rule form is unavailable, so the group is the only non-inventing option. Statements 4 and 5 of the review pull in opposite directions on the same shape; the plural rule settles it against the flat group-level property.
